rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods <U+2013> two-season field experiment (2007<U+2013>08, 2008<U+2013>09) at BARI Gazipur, RCBD with three irrigation levels x three mulch treatments under drip, yield and water use measured. Q2: Results, 'Water use and water use efficiency' section and Figure 1 <U+2013> at 50% ETc, drip-irrigated plots mulched with polyethylene gave the highest WUE of 592 kg/ha/mm (= 59.2 kg/m3), higher than straw mulch (581) or no mulch; abstract repeats this figure.
rows.notes: The study reports exactly the figure the passage attributes to it. However, all treatments were drip-irrigated (no furrow/other-method control), so the high WUE reflects deficit irrigation plus polyethylene mulch under drip rather than an isolated effect of drip itself. Seasonal water use was computed from CROPWAT ETc rather than measured; no soil evaporation or soil moisture was measured (mechanism asserted only). Single site, single crop, plot scale. Table 2 gives CV and LSD for yield but no dispersion measure for WUE; no limitations stated; no conditions for the effect stated as requirements beyond observing larger mulch effect at lower irrigation regime.
